conflicts.description: The Vellum Court seeks to prove a disputed heir's claim before the next toll changes the crypt record again, while the Giltwake Compact profits by financing both sides. The Drowned Cantors may know why the name shifted, but revealing it could expose a bargain on which the whole city depends.
conflicts.name: The Unwritten Heir

description: Far below the sea, where a trench cuts the ocean floor like a wound, merchants and noble houses bargain in the flooded remains of a cathedral. Its towers shelter markets, its crypts hold old debts, and its bells toll without hands when the trench currents turn. In this mysterious fantasy world, wealth is measured not only in coin but in the pressure a family can withstand—and the secrets it can keep sealed.

factions.description: A league of merchant families that controls the safest routes through the trench and lends pressure-suited divers to anyone who can pay. Its members collect debts in favors, especially favors owed during a bell toll.
factions.name: The Giltwake Compact

factions.description: An alliance of old noble houses that claims the cathedral's crypts as ancestral property. The court maintains its authority through genealogies etched into salt, though rival branches quietly dispute what those records say.
factions.name: The Vellum Court

factions.description: Keepers of the cathedral's silent rites, these masked interpreters listen to the bells and record their patterns. They insist the tolls are warnings from the city itself, not omens to be bought or sold.
factions.name: The Drowned Cantors

history.description: A coastal kingdom carried its cathedral into the trench to escape a war above the waves. The congregation vanished during the descent, but the bells continued to sound.
history.name: The Last Procession

history.description: Merchant divers established the first permanent exchange in the choir shaft, recording every debt on salt tablets to survive the crushing depth.
history.name: The First Ledger

history.description: A noble heir found their family descent altered in the crypt records after a toll. The Vellum Court blamed the Cantors; the Cantors claimed the stone had corrected a lie.
history.name: The Shifted Lineage

locations.description: The cathedral's vast central nave, roofed by a shimmering pressure membrane and crowded with counting houses, stalls, and noble galleries. At each tide-turn, the buried bells sound through the stone; contracts made during the toll are considered binding even if no witness remembers signing them.
locations.name: Bellward Nave

locations.description: A maze of submerged burial chambers where pale mineral growth preserves the names of the dead. Families store sealed ledgers here, trusting that salt will keep ink and secrets intact, though some inscriptions change after the bells ring.
locations.name: The Salt Crypt

locations.description: A circular shaft descending from the cathedral's former choir loft to a vent of warm water. Traders exchange rare trench goods on suspended platforms, while couriers ride the updrafts carrying messages that can be heard by anyone willing to risk the pressure.
locations.name: Choirwell Exchange

name: The Sunk Choir

rules.statement: An oath spoken beneath the cathedral's central dome becomes physically painful to break until the next bell toll.
When the buried bells sound, trench currents reverse for a few minutes and carry loose objects toward the nave.
Names and agreements written in the Salt Crypt remain legible for centuries, but a bell toll can alter one letter in any record.
No one may enter a public market without a pressure suit or a sponsor who accepts liability for their safety.
